report.verdict: Your work on payouts and ledger services caught my attention, and ledger-recon makes the payments connection stronger. I read to the end still wondering what you built or changed at Northwind Pay.
write_up: Senior backend engineering in payments is the thread here. It’s common to see a current job reduced to one line and an earlier job left blank, but that leaves a recruiter guessing about the work behind the titles.

The strongest detail is in Projects: ledger-recon names the library, Go, its 1,200 GitHub stars and its use by three payment companies. That’s a useful model for naming the work, though your part in the project isn’t stated.

Start with what you did on Northwind Pay’s payouts and ledger services, then bring the payments specialty into your headline and the project into your About. A recruiter hiring for money movement could then see both the field you work in and your part in it.

fit.note: “Senior Backend Engineer” is in your headline and current title. “Payouts” and “ledger” are in your current job, while “reconciliation” is in Projects. “Go” is in Top Skills and Projects, and “PostgreSQL” and “Kafka” are in Top Skills. The posting’s “Money Movement,” “idempotent,” “on-call,” “technical design reviews,” “reliability” and “double-entry accounting” are not on your profile. Add them only if they describe your work: Money Movement belongs in the headline, and the others belong in the current job description. Move your payouts and ledger specialty into the headline first.
